defectSummary: The canonical set is uniquely defensible from the standalone stem and does not depend on the sibling case. The rationale nevertheless includes nonessential sibling-only details—left-basilar findings, actual urine-output/lactate trends, clinical icterus, and a fuller cholestatic laboratory pattern—which create scope leakage without changing rankability.

reasoning: The standalone independently establishes acute gallstone pancreatitis, systemic inflammatory deterioration, bilirubin elevation, and a dilated CBD containing a distal stone. Those facts uniquely support C3, urgent infection escalation with cultures and ordered empiric antibiotics, and urgent ERCP preparation. The provided urine output, temperature, and WBC also independently support P3 and P1 as monitoring parameters. Sibling details strengthen and explain the same selections but are not required. Missing pulmonary, necrosis, and pre-ERCP CT premises appropriately weaken distractors rather than making the item underdetermined. Because no canonical target relies on an imported fact and the blind records agree with the canonical set, no higher-precedence failure or reviewer-disagreement condition is satisfied.
